source.title: Adaptive Regularization via Residual Smoothing in Deep Learning Optimization
source.authors: Jung-Kyun Cho; Junseok Kwon; Byung-Woo Hong

record.tranche_reason: Compares adaptive optimizers with SGD on image-classification validation accuracy, using different models and datasets from the version’s cited comparison.
record.gate_note: Table 3 reports validation accuracy for SGD, Adam, and AdaGrad. Its proposed residual-smoothing method and label smoothing are also compared, but those results do not test a listed version. The paper reports training curves, but no comparative training-accuracy values for the optimizer comparison.
record.test_reason: Table 3 directly compares held-out classification accuracy under SGD, Adam and AdaGrad, testing V4 with the same kind of optimizer comparison and measure as its original source. Different architectures do not constitute a different method. The study is not an original source for V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors conclude that residual-dependent smoothing with combined local and global adaptivity improves image-classification generalization in their experiments. Integration into other deep-learning applications is proposed as potential, rather than demonstrated.
record.recipe_differences: The optimizer comparison uses ResNet56 and DenseNet-BC on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and SVHN, with the paper’s stated common training setup and recommended optimizer parameters; it does not reproduce the cited optimizer study’s benchmark sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The optimizer comparison varies model, dataset, and optimizer; Adam’s difference from SGD is much smaller on ResNet56/SVHN than on the CIFAR settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Residual smoothing exceeds the SGD baseline on the recorded peak-accuracy metric in all six architecture–dataset settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive residual smoothing can improve validation accuracy over SGD under the tested configurations.

record.problems: The optimizer comparison reports five-trial maximum and mean validation accuracy but no uncertainty estimates or significance tests. It does not report comparative training accuracy or broad hyperparameter tuning for the compared optimizers.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 also reports mean validation accuracy for the same optimizer and regularization conditions; those additional metric rows are omitted to keep the extraction focused on the table’s maximum validation accuracy metric. Tables 1 and 2 report further residual-smoothing versus weight-decay validation results on Fashion-MNIST, including partial training sets, which are outside the tested listed versions and omitted.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps, zero-training-error thresholds and continued generalization beyond those thresholds.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.

Language benchmarks; equal or better training performance of adaptive optimizers; systematic learning-rate and schedule tuning; broader tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD. Recommended optimizer parameters are mentioned, but optimizer-specific settings and tuning searches are not adequately documented.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations that recover large-batch performance.
Dropout comparisons, small-data exceptions, excessive dropout and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness and its association with generalization gaps or ranking against alternative measures.
Removal of memorized examples compared with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: All recorded numerical values and architecture assignments match Table 3. Its max metric is an average of five within-trial epoch maxima; its mean metric averages the final 10% of epochs and then averages over trials. Omitted mean results are explicitly declared in rows_left_out and also place Adam and AdaGrad below SGD in every setting. No uncertainty estimates or significance tests are supplied. The optimizer comparison supports a recipe-specific held-out performance difference; it does not establish that adaptive optimizers fit training data equally well or received comparable tuning.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not tested.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No language benchmarks, broader optimizer tuning, switching from Adam to SGD, or decoupled weight decay comparison.
